questions.question: What is a "lingua franca"?
options: A common language used between people with different mother tongues
The official language of France
A dead language like Latin
A secret language used by traders
questions.explanation: A lingua franca is a shared language used for communication between people who have different mother tongues. English is the world's most important lingua franca.

questions.question: Which historical factor helped make English a world language?
options: The British Empire spread English to colonies around the world
English was the easiest language to learn
The United Nations banned other languages
English was invented for international trade
questions.explanation: The British Empire spread English across the globe, and later the economic and cultural power of the USA strengthened its position.

questions.question: Which modern factor strengthens the position of English today?
options: The internet, technology and global popular culture
English has become the official language of every country
Other languages are disappearing by law
English grammar was simplified by international agreement
questions.explanation: The internet, technology, science, business and entertainment all use English heavily, which keeps strengthening its global role.

questions.question: A Japanese and a Brazilian businessperson meet. Which language will they most likely use?
options: English
Japanese
Portuguese
Spanish
questions.explanation: English functions as the world's lingua franca, so people with different mother tongues typically communicate in English.

questions.question: What does it mean that English has many "varieties"?
options: English is spoken differently in different places, like British, American and Indian English
English has many different alphabets
There are many ways to spell every English word
English changes completely every generation
questions.explanation: English exists in many varieties around the world - British, American, Australian, Indian and more - each with its own pronunciation and vocabulary.
